chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Salih ibn al-Sindi, from Ja‘far ibn Bashir, from ‘Ali ibn Abi Hamzah, from Abu Basir, from Abu Ja‘far عليه السلام.
“Then set your face for the religion, upright.”
He عليه السلام said: “It is the Wilayah.”

key_terms.الدِّينِ: The religion; the divinely ordained way
key_terms.الْوَلَايَةُ: The Wilayah; divinely mandated authority and guardianship
key_terms.تَعَالَى: Exalted is He; a declaration of Allah’s transcendence
key_terms.حَنِيفًا: Upright and inclining purely to the truth
key_terms.فَأَقِمْ: So set firmly; establish and direct steadfastly
key_terms.قَوْلِهِ: His saying, referring to the divine statement being interpreted

ai.seo_question: How did Imam Abu Ja‘far عليه السلام interpret “فَأَقِمْ وَجْهَكَ لِلدِّينِ حَنِيفًا” in relation to Wilayah?
ai.summary: This narration explains the Qur’anic phrase about setting one’s face toward the upright religion as referring to al-Wilayah. In this tafsir, the verse is understood to indicate devoted adherence to the divinely appointed authority and guardianship central to the religion.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from Salih Bin Al Sindy, from Ja’far Bin Bashir, from Ali Bin Abu Hamza, from Abu Baseer, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup>
regarding the Words of the Exalted
[30:30] Then set your face for the upright Religion.
en.sarwar: 35. A number of our people has narrated Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ibrahim al-Hamadani in a marfu‘ manner from abu ‘Abdallah (a.s.)
about the words of Allah, the Most High.
“We shall set up the balance to maintain proper justice on the Day of Judgment. . .” [21:47]
The Imam (a.s.) said, “Balances are the prophets and the executors of their wills.”
